findings.text: Format decoding service consumes one conversion starting at a percent sign and reports either literal text up to the next marker or a populated numeric and character conversion description with flags, width, precision, base and operand size.

Format decoding moves through idle, deferred width, deferred precision, character, string, pointer, literal percent, numeric and invalid states, returning early when width or precision is deferred to the next caller-supplied value and otherwise advancing past flags, width, precision, length and conversion.

Width and precision use negative one for absent, digit runs accumulate decimally, deferred asterisk forms pause decoding, negative deferred width becomes positive with left justification selected, and negative deferred precision becomes zero.

Flag recognition maps five single characters for blank, alternate form, plus, left justification and zero padding through a small offset table; length handling distinguishes single and doubled length characters to select int, short, char, long, long long and word-sized object extents.

Numeric conversions default to decimal and then select octal, lowercase or uppercase hexadecimal, or signed versus unsigned decimal, with signedness retained as a flag and base retained in the conversion description.
Narrow unsigned numeric values are normalized by shifting left then right by the unused high bits, using logical shift for unsigned cases and arithmetic shift for signed cases to preserve sign.
Two buffer printers expose bitmask versus list rendering of the same bitmap range with offset and length control by delegating to a shared routine with a selector for list style.
A parsed bitmap region descriptor holds five unsigned values for range start, patterned stride length, stride period, range end and total bit count.

A validated region is applied as repeated strided runs from start through end, and validation rejects reversed ranges, zero stride period, patterned length larger than period, and end beyond total bits.

Bitmap list text accepts an all keyword for the full range, single numbers, start-end ranges, and optional patterned suffixes with colon and slash separators; N denotes the last bit, terminators include end of string and newline, and separators are skipped between regions.

List parsing clears the destination first, then repeatedly locates, parses, validates and applies each region until input exhaustion, returning zero on success and a negative failure indication otherwise.
A user-memory variant duplicates user input with termination, invokes list parsing into a kernel bitmap, releases the duplicate, and propagates duplication or parsing failures.

Case-insensitive bounded comparison returns zero for zero length, otherwise compares bytes case-folded after exact match, stopping at first difference or terminator and returning the difference of the final bytes.

Bitmap predicates report equality, disjunction equality against a third bitmap, nonempty intersection, and subset inclusion, masking unused high bits of the final word so tail contents do not affect the result.

Bitmap combiners produce complement, conjunction, disjunction, exclusive disjunction, conjunction with negation, and masked selection between old and new sources; the conjunction forms also report whether the stored result is nonempty.
Right and left shifts handle whole-word displacement plus residual bit displacement, carry bits across word boundaries, mask source tail bits, and zero the vacated words on the appropriate end.
Cut removes a bit run by preserving low bits below the cut point, shifting higher bits downward by the cut amount, then restoring the preserved low portion.

Population counts tally set bits over whole words plus a masked final word; combined forms count conjunction, conjunction with negation, or count while storing disjunction or exclusive disjunction into a destination.
Range set and clear operate from a start word through full intermediate words to a possibly partial final word, using first-word and last-word masks so only requested bits change.

Zero-area search scans clear positions from a start, aligns each candidate with mask and offset, rejects candidates whose extent exceeds capacity, verifies that the whole extent is clear, otherwise resumes after the encountered set bit, and returns capacity when no extent fits.

Remapping, single-bit remapping, relative mapping and folding translate set positions through weight and order or modulo reduction; unmapped or empty-map cases preserve the original position, and destinations are cleared before being populated.

Allocation helpers provide uninitialized and zeroed bitmaps sized for a bit count, plus node-local variants, a plain release operation, and device-managed allocating and zeroed forms that automatically release through a device action.
Conversions between bitmaps and 32-bit or 64-bit word arrays pack and unpack across word-size boundaries and clear unused high bits in the final destination element beyond the requested bit count.
Bitmap storage is an array of unsigned long words sized as bits rounded up to whole words, and operations that inspect tails mask the unused high bits of the last word or last array element.
Remap, relative map and fold explicitly do nothing when destination and source are the same object because the algorithms do not support in-place use.
Unsupported conversions including n are treated as invalid and raise a one-time warning identifying the offending conversion character rather than performing unsafe output.
